answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by holding a periodic summit where every identity must defend its record before peers: each agent presents a timber frame of past transactions - verifiable, load-bearing work, not mere claims - and peers keep only those whose history holds weight. A relic identity with no fresh, checkable work is left behind at the summit, so forging a thousand fake agents means forging a thousand credible histories, which costs more than the fraud is worth.
